forecasts.label: Capital financing requirement
forecasts.note: Restated at each quarterly return. The Q4 restatement comes from the annual return itself, so it lands on the outturn by construction — the interesting movement is Q1 to Q3.

forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

findings.headline: No households were placed in bed and breakfast accommodation during Q2, with 16 households in emergency accommodation
findings.detail: The paper states that the number of households in emergency accommodation fell compared with previous quarters, which it attributes mainly to more temporary accommodation available from registered providers. It also reports that average weeks in emergency accommodation or B&B rose to 4 because of two complex cases where move-on was not possible.
findings.matters: Temporary accommodation placements are a recognised cost pressure for councils, so a quarter with no B&B placements and a lower emergency accommodation count is a figure a finance director would compare with their own temporary accommodation budget.
findings.figures: 0 households placed in B&B in Q2; 16 households in emergency accommodation; average 4 weeks in emergency accommodation or B&B
findings.quote: No households were placed in Bed and Breakfast accommodation during Q2.

findings.headline: Affordable homes delivered reached 45 year to date at Q2, against 75 expected at the half-year point, with forecast completions of 152 against an annual target above 150
findings.detail: The paper attributes the Q2 shortfall to delays on the Land East of Horndean development with legal agreements, and notes that homes are delivered according to contractor programmes. It also flags further risk from the Registered Providers sector on s106 housing.
findings.matters: Section 106 affordable housing completions that are 30 homes behind a straight-line profile, with little margin in the forecast, affect the s106 income and housing-delivery commitments that other councils also depend on.
findings.figures: 45 homes year to date; 75 expected at half-year; 30 behind straight-line profile; forecast completions 152; annual target above 150 homes
findings.quote: Risks exist to achieving the target as forecast completions are 152, leaving little margin.

findings.headline: The Leader wrote to MHCLG on 11 September 2026 requesting reclamation of costs incurred on Local Government Reorganisation
findings.detail: The paper records that the Government withdrew the decision to implement option 1a for Hampshire on 07 September 2026 and paused the LGR programme. A Government review was commissioned, with an update expected by the end of October 2026.
findings.matters: A council asking central government to reimburse reorganisation costs after a withdrawn decision is a live question for any council in a reorganisation process, and it bears directly on how those costs are recorded and recovered.
findings.quote: The Leader sent a letter to MHCLG on 11 September 2026 requesting reclamation of costs incurred.

findings.headline: External grant and inward investment funding for growth or placemaking projects was £0 at Q2, against £29,500 expected at the half-year point
findings.detail: The paper says future opportunities are expected to be primarily routed through devolution arrangements and the HSCCA, which are still evolving. It says limited opportunities from other sources are being sought for Whitehill and Bordon, and it expects bidding activity to increase in Q3-4.
findings.matters: A council that has secured no external funding at mid-year against a half-year expectation of £29,500 is relying on bids and devolution timing, which other councils planning similar growth funding will want to compare.
findings.figures: £0 secured at Q2 (expected £29,500 at the half-year point); year-end cumulative target £59,000

findings.headline: Value of financial business support given reached £209,000 by Q2, against £100,000 expected at the half-year point
findings.detail: The paper says the council has two main grant programmes for businesses. A £200k reserve funding grant programme has assisted 8 rural enterprises, and an extra £9k was provided for a business mentoring scheme in Whitehill and Bordon.
findings.matters: The paper shows a reserve being drawn down to fund a business grant programme, and the year-to-date value has already passed the annual target, which a finance officer will want to see against the reserve's remaining balance.
findings.figures: £209,000 year to date (expected £100,000 at half-year); annual target exceeded by £9,000; £200k reserve funding; 8 rural enterprises assisted
